questions.question: Which tag contains ALL other HTML elements?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <html> tag is the root element that wraps EVERYTHING else in an HTML document. All other tags must be inside it.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Where does visible webpage content go?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <body> section contains ALL visible content that users see in their browser window. The <head> contains invisible metadata.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <body> section contains ALL visible content that users see in their browser window. The <head> contains invisible metadata.

questions.question: What is the purpose of <!DOCTYPE html>?
options: To add a title to the page

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser that this is an HTML5 document and helps it render the page correctly. It's a declaration, not a tag!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Which section contains the page title?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <title> tag, which sets what appears in the browser tab, goes inside the <head> section along with other metadata.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: True or False: Content inside <head> appears on the webpage.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: False! Content inside the <head> section is never visible on the webpage itself. It's for behind-the-scenes information like page titles, character encoding, and CSS links.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: False! Content inside the <head> section is never visible on the webpage itself. It's for behind-the-scenes information like page titles, character encoding, and CSS links.

questions.question: What appears in the browser tab?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The text inside the <title> tag appears in the browser tab, bookmarks, and search engine results. It's like the name tag for your webpage!

questions.question: Which comes first in an HTML document?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <!DOCTYPE html> always comes first in an HTML document. The order is: <!DOCTYPE>, then <html>, then <head>, then <body>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Which tag pair is ALWAYS required in HTML?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: While <head> and <body> are important, technically only <html> is absolutely required. However, good HTML should include all three!
